submission.summary: This 28-year-old female has active Dermatology problems including Hidradenitis suppurativa (diagnosed March 2020, Hurley stage II) and acne vulgaris treated with topical medications. She presented to Dermatology in January 2021 with progressive hair thinning on the crown consistent with female pattern hair loss. Relevant comorbidities include polycystic ovary syndrome with elevated testosterone (82 ng/dL, above normal range), obesity (BMI 36 kg/m²), and hirsutism with male-pattern facial hair distribution. She is currently prescribed Clindamycin phosphate 1% topical gel BID for acne and HS lesions. Her inflammatory markers (CRP 2 mg/L, ESR 15 mm/hr) were within normal limits at last evaluation. The combination of HS, acne, and androgenetic alopecia in the setting of PCOS and hyperandrogenism suggests a hormonal component to her dermatologic conditions.
